faq.a: Zaharah is associated with the Arabic form زَهْرَة, whose core sense is zaharah; blossom, flower (malay form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Zaharah?
faq.a: Zaharah is associated with Arabic. Zaharah is the Malay form of Arabic زَهْرَة (Zahra), meaning 'blossom, flower'.
Yes — the underlying form زَهْرَة is Arabic.
Zaharah can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Zaharah should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Zahra is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Zaharah mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Zaharah is rendered زہرہ and carries the sense زہرہ، پھول.

faq.q: What does Zaharah mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Zaharah is rendered زهره and carries the sense زهره، شکوفه.
A romanized syllable approximation is za-ha-rah. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Zaharah, zaharah. Script forms are زهره, زَهْرَة, زہرہ, ज़हरा.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
